about: A free archive extractor for Windows, macOS and Linux that unpacks ZIP, 7z, RAR and tar files in place.

prs.title: Unzipped files keep their real modification times
prs.broken: Files pulled out of a ZIP got times shifted by the computer's time zone, because the precise time stored in the archive was ignored.
prs.changed: The extractor now reads the precise time the archive stores, like other unzip tools do.
prs.matters: File dates stay correct, so backups and sorting by date still work after extracting.

prs.title: Archives with files dated before 1970 no longer crash the extractor
prs.broken: A tar archive holding a file dated before 1970 made the extractor crash while listing, testing or extracting it.
prs.changed: Old dates are now read correctly, and dates that cannot be shown are skipped instead of crashing.
prs.matters: Old archives, like scanned family photos or legacy backups, open without the tool falling over.

prs.title: Tar files keep dates before 1970 and far in the future
prs.broken: Files with very old or far future dates came out dated 1 January 1970, because the real date sits in an extra record.
prs.changed: Extraction now reads that record when it is there.
prs.matters: Extracted files keep their real modified dates.

prs.title: Extracted folders keep their permissions and dates
prs.broken: Only files got their permissions back. Every folder came out with default permissions and the time of extraction, though the docs promised otherwise.
prs.changed: Folders now get the permissions and modified time stored in the archive, even when an extraction is resumed.
prs.matters: Folders restored from an archive look the way they did when it was made.

prs.title: Names with a colon extract on Linux and macOS
prs.broken: Any name with a colon stopped a 7z or tar extraction with an error about writing outside the folder, including Wine prefixes and files like meeting 10:30.txt.
prs.changed: Colons are now allowed outside Windows, while names starting with a drive letter are still refused everywhere.
prs.matters: Archives holding these names extract fully, as they do with GNU tar and 7z.
